comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The current University of Twente curriculum page explicitly identifies its course-code and study-unit table as 2026-2027, defines four coherent 15-EC modules in each of years one and two, and gives year three as a 30-EC minor followed by 15 EC of thesis preparation and a 15-EC BSc thesis. The first year covers the construction, water, and traffic domains; the second year integrates delta safety, sustainable civil engineering, area development, and simulation and stochastic modelling. The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without inventing a choice. Every listed study unit and the minor account for exactly 180 EC. Fixed-queue review on 2026-10-16 rechecked the current 2026-27 curriculum and programme description. All settled components, EC and the neutral route decision are preserved. Related UCR programmes address environmental assessment and the ecological/social impacts of infrastructure without claiming civil-engineering design training.

alternatives.concept: Investigate water and delta risks through environmental geoscience, water governance, circular resource assessment and quantitative modelling. The programme combines field/GIS and geochemical tools with calculus, probability, numerical methods and data processing. It is a related environmental-science response to Civil Engineering, with engineering design, structures, hydraulics and transport remaining outside its coverage.

alternatives.labelRationale: Sixteen environmental, water, resource and sustainability courses and seven mathematical/computational courses define the curriculum. Water and delta risk provide the application; quantitative environmental assessment is substantial. No structural, hydraulic or transport-engineering sequence is implied.

alternatives.concept: Assess how infrastructure decisions affect coastal ecosystems, water, resources and communities, combining nature-based solutions, environmental field methods, circular resource and energy assessment, governance, environmental justice and stakeholder research. This is a related sustainability programme rather than construction or transport engineering.

alternatives.labelRationale: Nineteen environmental, ecology, water and resource courses form the core. Four sociology, research-method and communication courses address the evidenced social impacts and public choices around infrastructure, plus mandatory PPD. The label identifies infrastructure as the application of an environmental programme and does not imply civil-engineering design training.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Eight courses / 60 EC differ in each direction. The second programme replaces seven mathematics/computing courses and Earth System Science Tools with biodiversity, ecosystems, marine ecology, renewable-system assessment, sociology, qualitative stakeholder inquiry, environmental justice and climate communication. This materially shifts the programme from quantitative environmental analysis to ecological consequences and collective infrastructure decisions.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Environmental and mathematical gateways precede dependent advanced study. Dynamic Earth and Building with Nature precede the water, GIS and aquifer courses; Python and Mathematical Methods precede numerical methods; linear algebra precedes numerical methods and advanced calculus. The sustainability material-science gateway precedes recovery/remediation and resource research. Exact planned terms and all formal prerequisites pass.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related programmes are included sequentially. A third traffic/transport direction cannot sustain a complete target-linked programme: mathematics, Python, numerical analysis and probability can supply general modelling methods, but the catalogue lacks traffic-flow theory, transport demand, network/transport policy and transport-design project sequences. Robotics path planning is autonomous motion planning, not traffic engineering, and algorithm courses alone would change the concept to computing. Construction concerns are covered only through material sustainability, nature-based solutions and impacts in ucr-2; no structural, geotechnical, fluid-mechanics or construction-design substitute is claimed.
